project.name: DoomsGame
project.description: Iron Man vs Doctor Doom Tower Defense game in C++17 and OpenGL 3.3, built for DMET502 Lab 2

nodes.name: Audio.cpp
nodes.summary: miniaudio-based audio manager providing music playback, SFX, and voice line support with per-channel volume controls.

nodes.name: Audio.h
nodes.summary: Header declaring the Audio namespace interface: init, shutdown, music control, SFX and voice playback functions.

nodes.name: Background.cpp
nodes.summary: OpenGL-based background renderer that loads up to 5 switchable textures, draws fullscreen quads, and provides a thumbnail picker UI for background selection.

nodes.name: Background.h
nodes.summary: Declares the Background class managing texture loading, rendering, thumbnail picking, and split-screen menu drawing.

nodes.name: WaveSystem.cpp
nodes.summary: Wave spawning engine implementing a 3-wave schedule (3, 5, 10 enemies), random lane assignment, enemy lifecycle management, and OpenGL rendering infrastructure from the integrated teammate codebase.
nodes.languageNotes: This file is byte-identical to the teammate's main.cpp and contains its own OpenGL setup, shader compilation, and render loop alongside the wave system logic.

nodes.name: gl.h
nodes.summary: GLAD v2 OpenGL 3.3 Core function loader — provides GL function pointers for the renderer via gladLoadGL().
nodes.languageNotes: Auto-generated C header; loads all GL 1.0-4.0 entry points through a user-supplied proc-address callback.

nodes.name: main.cpp
nodes.summary: Application entry point that initialises GLFW, loads GLAD, bootstraps the Game object, Audio, Background, and Cutscene systems, then runs the main render/event loop.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Initialises the miniaudio engine, loads the background music file, sets it looping and starts playback.

nodes.name: shutdown
nodes.summary: Releases all miniaudio sound and engine resources on exit.

nodes.name: playVoice
nodes.summary: Plays a one-shot voice line, optionally interrupting a currently playing one; reloads the voice sound from file each call.

nodes.name: playSfx
nodes.summary: Fires a one-shot sound effect through the miniaudio engine without tracking the instance.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Compiles the background GLSL shader program, sets up VAO/VBO geometry, and loads all provided background textures via stb_image.

nodes.name: draw
nodes.summary: Renders the currently selected background texture as a letterboxed fullscreen quad, with optional dimming.

nodes.name: drawPicker
nodes.summary: Draws the background selection picker UI overlay showing thumbnail quads for each loaded background, highlighting the hovered one.

nodes.name: drawMenuSplit
nodes.summary: Renders a split-screen main menu layout with two background images side-by-side, used for the Iron Man vs Doctor Doom hero selection screen.

nodes.name: quad
nodes.summary: Low-level helper that uploads uniform values and issues a single textured quad draw call.

nodes.name: Background
nodes.summary: Encapsulates OpenGL background rendering state: shader program, texture array, current selection index, and all draw/pick/split methods.

nodes.name: updateWaveSystem
nodes.summary: Per-frame wave controller: advances the wave schedule by time, spawns the next enemy when the inter-spawn interval elapses, and transitions to the next wave when all enemies are defeated.

nodes.name: spawnEnemy
nodes.summary: Spawns a single enemy of the given type on a random lane, capping the active enemy count per lane.

nodes.name: getWaveEnemyType
nodes.summary: Returns the EnemyType for the nth enemy in a given wave based on the hardcoded wave schedule (Easy/Medium/Hard distribution).

nodes.name: addEnemy
nodes.summary: Appends an Enemy record to the global enemy list and delegates spawning of the matching Game Unit to the Game layer.

nodes.name: removeDefeatedEnemies
nodes.summary: Erases all inactive enemy records from the global enemy vector using erase-remove idiom.

nodes.name: Characters.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements geometry helper functions for character units — computing display scale, draw height, and half-width from a CharacterDef, with unitHalfWidth delegating to unitScale for consistent sizing.

nodes.name: Characters.h
nodes.summary: Declares the CharacterDef struct and EnemyType/CharType enums that define all six unit types (three heroes and three enemies) with their cost, HP, speed, damage, and animation frame data.

nodes.name: Config.h
nodes.summary: Centralizes shared game constants in the cfg namespace — lane count, board pixel dimensions, coin value, physics/timing constants — plus an inline laneBottom helper for Y-coordinate lookup.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a C++ namespace (cfg) to scope constants, avoiding global pollution while keeping definitions header-only.

nodes.name: Game.h
nodes.summary: Central game header declaring all runtime entity structs (Unit, Projectile, Collectible, RewardPopup, Explosion) and the Game class that owns every subsystem, state machine, and per-frame update/render loop.
nodes.languageNotes: Acts as the monolithic aggregation header; all subsystem headers are pulled in here, so translation units that include Game.h get the full game API.

nodes.name: Renderer.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the OpenGL 3.3 batched sprite renderer: shader compilation, single VAO/VBO sprite atlas upload, letterboxed viewport management, and all draw primitives (rect, sprite, pixel-font text with shadows/outlines).
nodes.languageNotes: Embeds a 5×7 bitmap font as a baked glyph table and uses GLM for matrix math; all draw calls go through a single VAO for minimal GL state changes.

nodes.name: UI.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements all visual elements: the hero card-bar HUD, animated battlefield grid with per-background environment art (floor and edge layers), coin panel, health bars, and text helpers used by Game screens.

nodes.name: UI.h
nodes.summary: Declares the CardBar struct and free-function prototypes for the battlefield drawing API (drawBattlefield, drawCoinPanel, drawHealthBar, drawCenteredText) used by Game::render.

nodes.name: unitScale
nodes.summary: Returns a float scale factor for a character unit based on its CharacterDef role, used to map logical grid units to pixel size.

nodes.name: unitHeight
nodes.summary: Returns the pixel draw height for a unit from its CharacterDef, used by the renderer to place sprites at the correct lane baseline.

nodes.name: unitHalfWidth
nodes.summary: Returns the half-width of a unit's sprite in pixels, computed from sprite columns multiplied by unitScale, used for collision and centering.

nodes.name: CharacterDef
nodes.summary: Plain data struct describing a character type's tuning values: display name, role, unlock/battle cost, max HP, movement speed, damage, attack cooldown, sprite frame offset, and draw height.

nodes.name: laneBottom
nodes.summary: Inline helper returning the pixel Y coordinate of a lane's bottom edge, computed from board geometry constants in the cfg namespace.

nodes.name: Unit
nodes.summary: Runtime state struct for a live game unit (hero or enemy): holds a CharacterDef pointer, lane index, x position, current HP, attack/animation timers, jump offset, and flags for fighting/reachedBase/exited.

nodes.name: Projectile
nodes.summary: Represents a projectile in flight: lane, current and previous X, vertical offset, velocity, owner flag (fromEnemy), trajectory type (high), damage, and alive status.

nodes.name: Collectible
nodes.summary: Represents a coin drop collectible on the battlefield: lane, x position, lifetime age, and alive flag.

nodes.name: RewardPopup
nodes.summary: Floating coin-reward popup for visual feedback: lane, x, coin amount, and age used to fade/rise the number over time.

nodes.name: Explosion
nodes.summary: Timed explosion effect struct: lane, x/y position, age, and DURATION constant used to animate blast frames.

nodes.name: Game
nodes.summary: Central game controller owning all entity collections (units, projectiles, collectibles, explosions), the state machine, Renderer, UI, Cutscene, and Audio references, plus all per-frame update/render methods and input handlers.

nodes.name: compileShader
nodes.summary: Compiles a GLSL vertex or fragment shader from source, checks compilation status, and prints info-log on failure, returning the shader handle.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Initializes the renderer: compiles and links the sprite shader program, queries uniform locations, creates the shared VAO/VBO, and builds the glyph table from the embedded 5×7 bitmap font.

nodes.name: shutdown
nodes.summary: Releases all OpenGL resources (VAO, VBO, shader program) created during init.

nodes.name: addSprite
nodes.summary: Builds GPU vertex data for a multi-row pixel-art sprite sheet, appending quad vertices and UV coordinates into the shared vertex buffer for later upload.

nodes.name: upload
nodes.summary: Uploads the accumulated vertex data to the GPU VBO and configures vertex attribute pointers for position and UV, completing renderer initialization after all sprites are added.

nodes.name: beginFrame
nodes.summary: Sets up each frame: clears the framebuffer, computes the letterboxed viewport to maintain aspect ratio, enables alpha blending, binds the shader, and sets the orthographic projection matrix.

nodes.name: draw
nodes.summary: Core draw call: sets the model matrix, tint color, and red/gray uniforms, then issues a glDrawArrays call for the given sprite frame range.

nodes.name: drawRect
nodes.summary: Draws a solid-color rectangle by constructing a scale+translate model matrix and calling draw with the white-rect sprite and given color/alpha.

nodes.name: drawSprite
nodes.summary: Draws a sprite frame at world coordinates with optional X-flip and draw-effect flags, composing the model matrix from position and scale.

nodes.name: drawText
nodes.summary: Renders a string using the 5×7 bitmap glyph table, drawing each character as a series of filled pixel rects at the requested pixel size and color.

nodes.name: drawTextStyled
nodes.summary: Extends drawText with per-glyph gradient (top/bottom colors), drop shadow at a configurable offset, and optional outline, used for styled title and HUD text.

nodes.name: textWidth
nodes.summary: Returns the pixel width of a string rendered at the given pixel size, used for horizontal centering calculations.

nodes.name: Glyph
nodes.summary: Internal struct mapping an ASCII character to its 5×7 bitmap row data, used to build the font atlas for drawText.

nodes.name: cardRect
nodes.summary: Returns the screen-space bounding rectangle for a card slot at index i in the CardBar, given the bar's origin.

nodes.name: hitTest
nodes.summary: Returns the card slot index (0-based) for a world-space mouse position, or -1 if no card was hit, used for hover and click handling in the card bar.

nodes.name: draw
nodes.summary: Renders the full card-bar HUD: draws card backgrounds and selection highlights, card portrait sprites, cost labels, and lock overlays for each of the available hero cards.

nodes.name: drawEnvironmentFloor
nodes.summary: Renders the themed floor layer for each battlefield lane using time-animated sinusoidal effects, with per-background visual variants (city, lab, arctic, etc.) drawn via drawRect primitives.

nodes.name: drawEnvironmentEdges
nodes.summary: Renders the foreground and background edge decoration layers for each battlefield lane (buildings, pillars, tech panels) with per-background variants and time-based animation.

nodes.name: drawBattlefield
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the complete battlefield render: lane highlight overlays, base HP indicators, the environment floor and edge layers, lane selection overlays, and the base structure sprites at each end.

nodes.name: drawCoinPanel
nodes.summary: Renders the coin counter HUD panel with coin icon sprite and right-aligned coin count text.

nodes.name: drawHealthBar
nodes.summary: Draws a health bar with background, filled portion in a colour interpolated from green to red, and a border, used for both player and enemy units.

nodes.name: drawCenteredText
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that horizontally centers a string on the screen at a given Y position using drawText and textWidth.

nodes.name: CardBar
nodes.summary: Struct representing the hero-purchase card bar HUD element, storing its screen origin and width, with methods for card hit-testing and rendering.

nodes.name: Cutscene.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the scripted 18-second intro cutscene with time-based animation helpers (lerp, prog, mix3) and procedural drawing routines that composite Iron Man and Doctor Doom characters with dialogue panels over the Renderer.
nodes.languageNotes: The monolithic draw() function (127-436) encodes the entire animation timeline as a series of time-windowed prog() calls, making it a fully self-contained scene description.

nodes.name: Cutscene.h
nodes.summary: Declares the Cutscene class with lifecycle methods (start, update, draw, skip, finished) and a fixed 18-second DURATION constant that controls the intro sequence.

nodes.name: EnemySprites.h
nodes.summary: Contains ASCII art pixel arrays and color palettes defining the visual appearance of the three Doombot enemy variants: Easy (Doombot), Medium (Heavy Doombot), and Hard (Melee Doombot).
nodes.languageNotes: Data-only header with no functions; each sprite variant is encoded as a char grid alongside a Palette initializer list consumed by buildSprites.

nodes.name: HeroSprites.h
nodes.summary: Contains ASCII art pixel arrays and color palettes for the three Iron Man hero unit types (Melee, Ranged, Defense), consumed by buildSprites to populate the Renderer's sprite atlas.
nodes.languageNotes: Data-only header mirroring EnemySprites.h in structure; each hero has multiple animation frames stored as separate char grids.

nodes.name: Renderer.h
nodes.summary: Declares the Renderer class providing an OpenGL 3.3 batched quad drawing system with support for colored rectangles, sprite rendering, and pixel-font text output, plus supporting structures for palettes, sprite frames, and draw effects.
nodes.languageNotes: Renderer uses a client-side vertex buffer (verts) flushed per-frame; addSprite/upload separate sprite registration from rendering to allow lazy GPU upload.

nodes.name: Sprites.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements buildSprites, which registers all hero and enemy sprite frames into the Renderer sprite atlas using the ADD_SPRITE macro against the ASCII art data from HeroSprites.h and EnemySprites.h.

nodes.name: Sprites.h
nodes.summary: Declares the buildSprites function interface and the sprite-index constants used to reference hero and enemy sprites by ID throughout the game.

nodes.name: drawDisc
nodes.summary: Draws a filled circle by stamping a square quad scaled by the circle radius; used for glowing arc-reactor and energy effects in the cutscene.

nodes.name: drawLine
nodes.summary: Renders a thick line segment as a rotated quad between two screen-space endpoints; used for beam and connector effects in the cutscene scenes.

nodes.name: drawUnit
nodes.summary: Draws a game unit sprite at a given screen position with optional horizontal flip, delegating to Renderer::drawSprite.

nodes.name: unitBox
nodes.summary: Draws a unit portrait inside a styled card box with configurable border sides; used to display character cards in the story dialogue panels.

nodes.name: draw
nodes.summary: Main cutscene rendering function encoding the full 18-second animated timeline as time-windowed drawing commands; composites backgrounds, characters, beams, dialogue boxes, and subtitle text in sequence.

nodes.name: Cutscene
nodes.summary: Controller class for the intro cutscene holding elapsed time t, a done flag, and the fixed DURATION constant; exposes start/update/draw/skip/finished lifecycle API.

nodes.name: Renderer
nodes.summary: Core OpenGL rendering class managing a batched vertex buffer; provides drawRect, drawSprite, drawText, and drawTextStyled for all 2D drawing in the game, plus addSprite/upload for sprite atlas management.

nodes.name: buildSprites
nodes.summary: Registers all hero and enemy sprite frames into the Renderer's atlas by invoking ADD_SPRITE for each ASCII art grid defined in HeroSprites.h and EnemySprites.h.

nodes.summary: Main project documentation for DoomsGame describing the Iron Man vs Doctor Doom tower defense game, covering features, C++17/OpenGL tech stack, architecture overview, build and run instructions, controls, screenshots, and known limitations.

nodes.name: glfw3.h
nodes.summary: Vendored GLFW 3.5.1 public API header providing window creation, OpenGL context management, input handling, and event callbacks for the game's windowing layer.
nodes.languageNotes: Third-party header; defines all GLFW constants, structs, and function declarations. Not modified by the project.

nodes.name: glfw3native.h
nodes.summary: Vendored GLFW native platform extension header exposing OS-level handles (HWND, HDC, etc.) for platform-specific window interop beyond the core GLFW API.

nodes.name: Game.cpp
nodes.summary: Core game logic implementation: manages the full Game class lifecycle including state machine (MainMenu, Playing, Won, Lost), unit placement, swept-segment projectile combat, coin economy, enemy wave integration, HUD rendering, and the animated main menu.

nodes.name: Template.vcxproj
nodes.summary: Visual Studio C++ project file configuring Debug/Release builds for Win32 and x64 platforms with C++17 standard, GLFW and OpenGL link dependencies, and include paths for the GLAD and External headers.

nodes.name: Template.vcxproj.filters
nodes.summary: Visual Studio filter file organizing project sources into Source Files, Header Files, and Assets groups for IDE navigation.

nodes.name: WaveSystem.h
nodes.summary: Declares the wave system interface: the Enemy struct, global state variables (enemies vector, currentWave, playerWon, etc.) and the updateWaveSystem / resetWaves / removeDefeatedEnemies functions that connect the teammate's WaveSystem.cpp to the main game loop.

nodes.name: khrplatform.h
nodes.summary: Khronos platform type definitions header providing portable integer type aliases and calling-convention macros required by GLAD and other OpenGL loader headers.

nodes.name: glad.h
nodes.summary: Vendored GLAD v1 OpenGL loader header declaring all OpenGL 1.0–4.6 function pointers and the gladLoadGL entry point; retained for src/glad.c compatibility but superseded by glad v2 (include/glad/gl.h) for the main project build.
nodes.languageNotes: GLAD v1 inline loader: gladLoadGL resolves function pointers at runtime via a callback. The project uses GLAD v2 (include/glad/gl.h) instead; this file is only compiled by src/glad.c which is excluded from the build.

nodes.name: glad.c
nodes.summary: Vendored GLAD v1 C source file implementing OpenGL function pointer loading; kept for reference but excluded from the project build as the project uses the GLAD v2 header (include/glad/gl.h) instead.
nodes.languageNotes: NOT included in Template.vcxproj ClCompile items. Uses include/glad/glad.h (v1); the active build uses include/glad/gl.h (v2).

nodes.name: resetWaves
nodes.summary: Implements the resetWaves function declared in WaveSystem.h; clears the enemy spawn queue, resets wave counters, and sets lastSpawnTime to the current GLFW time.

nodes.name: drawMenuButton
nodes.summary: Renders a stylized menu button with hover glow, border highlight, label text, and optional sub-label using the Renderer primitives; handles both primary and secondary button styles.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Resets all game state to a fresh playing session: clears units, projectiles, coins, explosions, resets economy counters, re-initialises unlocked cards, and calls resetWaves.

nodes.name: spawnEnemy
nodes.summary: Creates a new enemy Unit in the specified lane from an Enemy wave definition and pushes it into the enemies vector, positioning it at the right edge of the board.

nodes.name: placePlayer
nodes.summary: Places a hero unit in the chosen lane after spending coins, initialising its position, HP, and character definition and appending it to the players vector.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Main per-frame update dispatcher: advances the cutscene or the playing state, drives the wave system, spawns pending enemies into the game, delegates to updatePlayers/Enemies/Projectiles/Explosions and cleanup, and transitions to Won/Lost state.

nodes.name: updatePlayers
nodes.summary: Advances all hero units each frame: moves them toward blocking enemies, fires projectiles when in range, and applies melee attacks, triggering audio cues for shots and melee hits.

nodes.name: updateEnemies
nodes.summary: Advances all enemy units each frame: moves them left toward blocking heroes, applies melee damage on contact, and triggers coin spawning on enemy death.

nodes.name: updateProjectiles
nodes.summary: Moves all active projectiles and tests swept-segment collision against targets each frame, applying damage and spawning explosion effects on impact.

nodes.name: cleanup
nodes.summary: Removes dead units, spent projectiles, expired explosions, and collected coins from their respective vectors at the end of each frame, also calling removeDefeatedEnemies on the wave system.

nodes.name: onMouseMove
nodes.summary: Handles mouse movement to update hover states for card buttons and background thumbnails in the main menu and playing HUD.

nodes.name: onMouseButton
nodes.summary: Dispatches left-click events across all game states: background selection, volume controls, restart/menu buttons, card selection, and hero placement on board lanes.

nodes.name: onKey
nodes.summary: Handles keyboard shortcuts: skip cutscene, cycle backgrounds, restart game, and volume controls mapped to function and arrow keys.

nodes.name: drawUnit
nodes.summary: Renders a single hero or enemy unit scaled to its lane height with the correct sprite, optional horizontal flip, and a health bar overlay.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Full-frame renderer for the Playing, Won, and Lost states: draws the background, all units, projectiles, explosions, coin pickups, lane dividers, the card deck HUD, wave/score counters, and overlay screens for game-over and victory.

nodes.name: drawMainMenu
nodes.summary: Renders the full animated main menu including particle lightning bolts, animated Doom/Iron Man sprites, background thumbnail carousel, stylised title text, and the Play/Background/Volume control buttons.

nodes.name: gladLoadGLUserPtr
nodes.summary: GLAD v1 entry point that resolves all OpenGL function pointers using a user-supplied loader callback; called once after context creation to initialise the GL extension table.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: README.md is the best first stop for any newcomer: it names the game (Iron Man vs Doctor Doom Tower Defense), lists the tech stack (C++17, OpenGL 3.3, GLFW, GLAD, miniaudio, stb_image), and sketches the state machine flow from MainMenu through the cutscene to the Playing and Win/Loss states. Reading it first gives you the vocabulary — lanes, waves, Doombots, coin economy — that all subsequent source files assume you already know.

tour.title: Entry Point & Build Setup
tour.description: main.cpp is where execution starts: it calls GLFW to open a window, loads OpenGL function pointers via GLAD, constructs the Game object, and drives the per-frame loop that calls update and draw. Template.vcxproj declares every source file that Visual Studio compiles — checking it shows which .cpp files are in the build, what include paths are set, and that the project targets C++17 on x64. Together these two files answer 'how does the program start and how is it compiled?'
tour.languageLesson: C++ does not auto-discover source files. Template.vcxproj must list every .cpp file explicitly under <ClCompile> elements; a file you add to the folder but forget to add here will be silently ignored by MSBuild.

tour.title: Game Constants & Shared Types
tour.description: Config.h places all magic numbers in the cfg namespace — NUM_LANES=4, board bounds, COIN_VALUE, attack timings — so tuning the game means editing one file, not hunting through logic code. Characters.h defines the CharacterDef struct and the EnemyType/CharType enums that name all six unit types (three Iron Man heroes, three Doombot variants). These two headers are the vocabulary layer: every other module speaks in cfg:: constants and CharType values.
tour.languageLesson: C++ namespaces like cfg:: prevent name collisions and make constant origins self-documenting at the call site. Using 'constexpr' instead of '#define' gives the constant a type, scope, and debugger visibility.

tour.title: Central Game Header
tour.description: Game.h is the most-imported file in the codebase (fan-in 3): WaveSystem.cpp, UI.cpp, and main.cpp all include it. It declares the GameState enum (MainMenu, BgSelect, Cutscene, Playing, Won, Lost), and the core data structs — Unit, Projectile, Collectible, Explosion — that represent everything alive on the battlefield. Understanding these structs is essential before reading either Game.cpp or WaveSystem.cpp, because all combat and spawning logic operates by creating and mutating these objects.
tour.languageLesson: In C++, declaring structs and classes in a header and defining member functions in a .cpp separates interface from implementation. Any .cpp that includes Game.h gets the type layout without recompiling the method bodies.

tour.title: OpenGL Rendering Engine
tour.description: Renderer.h declares the Renderer class, which owns the single VAO and VBO that back every sprite drawn in the game, plus a 5x7 bitmap pixel font for HUD text. Renderer.cpp compiles a minimal GLSL vertex/fragment shader pair at startup, then every draw call batches textured quads into that one buffer and flushes with a single glDrawArrays call per frame. The letterboxed viewport logic ensures the game keeps its aspect ratio at any window size — a common technique in 2D games without an engine.
tour.languageLesson: Batched rendering collects all geometry for a frame into one CPU-side buffer, then uploads and draws it with a single GPU call. This avoids the per-draw overhead of binding different buffers or shaders and is why even simple 2D games outperform naive one-quad-per-draw approaches.

tour.title: Sprite Pipeline
tour.description: HeroSprites.h and EnemySprites.h store all character art as ASCII grid arrays paired with color palettes — each character is a compact, hand-authored pixel image. Sprites.h declares the buildSprites function and integer index constants (e.g. CH_MELEE, CH_EASY) that the rest of the code uses to reference a sprite by ID. Sprites.cpp implements buildSprites, which iterates those ASCII grids, converts each colored cell to two triangles, and uploads the geometry directly into the Renderer's VAO so sprites are ready to draw without any per-frame upload.
tour.languageLesson: Encoding artwork as ASCII character grids in C++ header files keeps the entire project self-contained with no external asset files. Each character maps to a palette color, so changing a palette entry recolors the whole sprite without touching the shape data.

tour.title: Core Game Logic
tour.description: Game.cpp is the largest file in the project and implements the full state machine: it handles mouse clicks on the card bar to place heroes, runs the per-frame update loop that moves projectiles using swept-segment collision detection, awards coins when enemies die, and transitions between states (Playing → Won when all waves are cleared, Playing → Lost when enemies cross the left edge). The coin economy — spending coins to place heroes, earning them from kills — is the core feedback loop that makes the game strategic.
tour.languageLesson: Swept-segment (or continuous) collision detection tests whether a moving object's path over one frame intersects a target, rather than checking its position only at the end of the frame. This prevents fast projectiles from tunneling through thin enemies.

tour.title: Wave Spawning Engine
tour.description: WaveSystem.h declares the global wave state and the three functions Game.cpp calls: updateWaveSystem(time) to tick the schedule, spawnEnemy(def, lane) to create a new Unit from a wave definition, and resetWaves() to restart on a new game. WaveSystem.cpp implements a three-wave schedule (3, 5, then 10 Doombots) with random lane assignment, escalating difficulty as the game progresses. The wave system is intentionally decoupled from Game.cpp: it owns the spawning schedule and writes new enemies into the shared enemies list, while Game.cpp owns their combat behavior.
tour.languageLesson: Keeping spawning logic in its own translation unit (WaveSystem.cpp) is a separation-of-concerns pattern. Game.cpp does not need to know the wave timing algorithm, and WaveSystem.cpp does not need to know how combat works — they communicate only through the shared Enemy list and the spawnEnemy/resetWaves interface.

tour.title: User Interface & Menus
tour.description: UI.h declares the CardBar struct (the bottom HUD showing placeable heroes and their coin costs) and all the drawing function prototypes for game screens. UI.cpp implements every player-facing screen: the animated battlefield grid, the card bar with locked/unlocked card rendering, and the full menu stack (main menu, settings, pause, win screen, loss screen). Because UI.cpp imports Game.h, it reads live game state each frame to reflect current health bars, coin totals, and unit positions.

tour.title: Visual Polish & Audio
tour.description: Background.h and Background.cpp add five switchable PNG backgrounds (selected before the game starts) using stb_image to load textures and a cover-fit shader to fill the viewport. Cutscene.h and Cutscene.cpp deliver an 18-second time-scripted intro that plays panel animations and fires audio cues before the first wave. Audio.h and Audio.cpp wrap the miniaudio library to provide looping background music, fire-and-forget sound effects, and voice lines — all three systems share the Audio namespace so any module can play a sound with a single function call.
tour.languageLesson: miniaudio is a header-only, single-file C audio library. Fire-and-forget SFX (triggering a sound and not tracking it) works by allocating a temporary sound object, starting it, and registering a callback that frees it on completion — no manual lifetime management needed in the caller.
